newsitem.title: USA: U.S. diplomat to visit Kabul in next few days.
newsitem.headline: U.S. diplomat to visit Kabul in next few days.

text.p: A U.S. diplomat will visit Kabul shortly to talk to the Taleban militia which has seized most of Afghanistan and assess prospects for re-staffing the U.S. embassy there, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"We are going to be sending an American diplomat into Kabul in the next couple of days to make contact with the Taleban," spokesman Nicholas Burns said. Citing security reasons, he declined to name the diplomat or say where he would be travelling from.
Burns said the diplomat's mission would be "to essentially investigate the situation in Kabul, see if a government is being formed" and pass on U.S. concerns about the Taleban's actions so far.

The aim was also "to see if at some point in the future it's wise to at least have embassy officials go back in and re-establish an American embassy presence in Kabul," he said. The United States never broke off relations with Afghanistan but evacuated its embassy there in 1989.

In Kabul, Taleban's acting Deputy Foreign Minister Sher Mohammed Stanakzai said the movement wanted good relations with neighbouring countries and with the United States and invited them to reopen their embassies in Kabul.

Burns on Tuesday reiterated U.S. concerns over Taleban's human rights practices, including its summary execution last week of former president Najibullah and its imposition of strict Islamic regulations on women.
